bull.b: The long-term Rockdale lease adds contracted infrastructure revenue beyond bitcoin mining and provides substantial visibility into future growth. Its targeted high NOI margin could improve earnings quality and diversify Riot toward more predictable data center economics as capacity is delivered.

Rapid engineering growth, expanding margins, and a sizable backlog indicate strengthening execution capabilities within Riot’s infrastructure platform. Greater vertical integration may support delivery of contracted data center projects, improve control over lead times, and create an additional revenue stream.

Low power and direct production costs provide an important operating advantage in a competitive mining market where network hash rate and difficulty can pressure margins. Efficient power management and 44.4 EH/s of deployed capacity support Riot’s ability to remain productive across market conditions.

bear.b: Large recurring losses and negative cash generation weaken financial resilience and reduce the company’s ability to fund expansion internally. Continued cash burn could require additional financing or asset sales, while poor current profitability makes execution more dependent on improving operating performance.

Riot’s contracted growth opportunity requires substantial upfront investment before the planned 2027–2028 deliveries generate rent. Large project spending and anticipated borrowing increase execution and financing demands, leaving returns sensitive to construction progress, funding terms, and timely tenant deployment.

Bitcoin mining remains a core earnings driver, exposing Riot to structural volatility from cryptocurrency prices and changing network competition. Even with efficient power costs, weaker bitcoin economics or rising difficulty can pressure revenue and cash generation while data center diversification is still being built.
